highlights.description: Content findings for recordings: rules for quotations checked against audio by several speech-to-text engines, and narration findings for a recording that doesn't say its script

added.description: `content.RuleQuoteAudioDisputed`, `content.RuleQuoteAudioMismatch` and `content.RuleQuoteAudioUnchecked` for quotations checked against recordings; `content.quote.notFound` covers a quotation not located in the recording

`content.NarrationIssue` and `content.RuleNarrationMismatch`: a recording, or one segment, that doesn't say its script, projected to a finding of type `narration` with the segment as its location and what the engines heard as transcript evidence; `content.Segment(f)` reads the segment back
`content.TypeClaim` and `content.TypeNarration` finding types

changed.description: `content.ClaimID(f)` returns "" for content findings of a type other than `claim`; findings with no type are still read as claim findings

documentation.description: Content domain: rules for quotations from recordings, and narration findings
README describes recordings and narration in the content domain

tests.description: Audio quotation rules, narration findings, and `ClaimID` for narration and untyped findings
Narration findings carry what the engines heard without modifying the caller's evidence

highlights.description: A `content` domain for the accuracy and attribution of published content: a claim its cited source does not support, a quotation not found in its source, a citation to an unreliable source. Claim checkers raise these findings and carry them through review with the shared status lifecycle

Security findings can now carry root cause, product impact, exploit notes, verification, typed relationships to work items and fixes, and a disclosure lifecycle, so one record spans discovery, engineering fix, and product impact
Findings render into a formal report that pandoc converts to DOCX or PDF, with a shareable audience that keeps exploit detail out

added.description: `findingspec`: typed `Relationship` links (threat, control, requirement, tracking item, fix, test, duplicate) and `Verification` on `Finding`
`security`: `RootCause`, `Impact`, `Exploit`, and `Publication` (visibility, disclosure state, GHSA/CVE/OSV/Go vulnerability IDs, affected version ranges) on `Vulnerability` and its `Detail`
`security`: `Exception.Rationale`, the approver's stated justification for accepting a risk, so an accepted vulnerability can be reported with its reason

`report`: render a `FindingSet` as a formal, pandoc-ready Markdown report (metadata block, executive summary, severity tables, linked findings overview, per-finding detail) for a shareable or internal audience; the shareable default omits exploit detail, evidence payloads, and code snippets
`findingspec`: `DomainContent`, for findings about claims and their sources

`content`: `Issue`, a problem with one claim or one of its sources, projected by `ToFinding` with the claim as the location (`Location.Component` the claim ID, `File` the document, `Snippet` the statement) and `claim:`/`source:` tags; `ClaimID` reads the claim back from a finding
`content`: twelve common rule IDs, from `content.evidence.none` and `content.quote.notFound` to `content.facts.missing` and `content.claim.singleSource`

documentation.description: Analysis, verification, and disclosure fields on security findings
Exception rationale in the security domain guide
Report reference page, README section, and navigation; report rendering in the PRD, TRD, and roadmap
Content domain guide with its rules and how a finding's status follows it through a review funnel
Documentation site uses the PlexusOne MkDocs theme and site navigation

highlights.description: Initial release — a domain-neutral model that normalizes findings across security, accessibility (a11y), internationalization (i18n), and quality engineering (qe) into one canonical `Finding` with a typed, per-type `Detail` subsection
Two-level `Domain` + `Type` taxonomy with ingest adapters for open-source scanners: gitleaks, axe-core, and govulncheck in-repo (Grype, Trivy, and AWS Inspector via their tool libraries)
Call-graph reachability (via govulncheck) as a first-class prioritization signal, and a canonical container/SCA package-vulnerability shape shared by Grype, Trivy, and Inspector

added.description: `findingspec`: canonical `Finding` and `FindingSet` with domain/severity/open filtering, counting, severity ordering, and a `Summary` analytics rollup

`findingspec`: shared vocabulary — `Severity` (via the priority-frameworks Severity framework), `Status`, `Confidence`, `Domain`, `Source`, `Location` (code, runtime, or RFC 6901 JSON Pointer), `Evidence`, `Remediation`, `Reference`
`findingspec`: typed per-type `Detail` subsection — `Finding.Type`, `SetDetail`, and generic `DetailAs[T]`

`security`: `Vulnerability` with inherent vs. residual severity, compensating controls, and exception-driven effective severity; `Secret`; `CVSS`; `Package`/`Fix`/`Artifact` for SCA and container scans; and call-graph `Reachability`
`a11y`: WCAG `Issue` with conformance level and impact-to-severity mapping
`i18n`: internationalization/localization `Issue` types
`qe`: quality-engineering `Failure` for end-to-end and user-journey findings
`adapters/gitleaks`: secret-scan JSON report to security/secret findings, with redaction and provider/kind inference
`adapters/axe`: axe-core results JSON to a11y/wcag findings, one per element, with WCAG criterion/level parsed from tags
`adapters/govulncheck`: `govulncheck -json` to security/sca findings, deriving call-graph reachability (state, vulnerable symbol, example call paths)
